patients.label: 60-year-old woman with ipsilateral left femoral neck and sub-trochanteric fractures after a traffic accident, treated with a long Gamma3 nail and later femoral head necrosis

identity_evidence.quote: A 60-year-old female patient met with a traffic accident while walking.

attribution_limitations: Source conflict on necrosis timing: the Abstract places evidence of necrosis "after 5 years", while the Case presentation (4-year follow-up), the Fig. 4 caption ("At 4 year follow-up") and the Discussion ("4 year postoperation") place it at 4 years, with arthroplasty one year after the X-ray. All timed necrosis statements are review_only; the untimed necrosis and X-ray result are kept.
The left lower limb "was tracting" and the right elbow "was casting"; the wording does not clearly say traction or a cast was applied.
The neurovascular examination sentence uses "His" although the patient is called a female patient and "she" elsewhere.

The authors list possible reasons for necrosis (possible injury to the medial circumflex femoral artery, late operation causing high articular pressure, a heavy load to the hip in a fat woman) with "might be"; operation timing is not stated elsewhere.
AIS 14 and ISS 27 are printed without defining the scales or any component scores; AIS is normally a per-region score, so "14" is kept exactly as printed.

The reference point of "after 2 weeks" for the transfer to the authors hospital is not stated (accident or admission to the nearby hospital). The Case presentation says surgery was performed "Eventually" and does not give the date or interval of surgery.

The Discussion and Conclusion contain general or hypothetical statements (a prosthetic replacement "may be an option", surveillance recommendations for patients with this fracture, reasons for choosing a Gamma3 nail) that are not documented care of this patient.

evidence.quote: AP radiographic reveal a ipsilateral left femoral neck and sub-trochanteric fracture.
The fracture was fixed by a long Gamma3 nail.
At 12-month follow-up, the fracture was union and has no evidence of avascular necrosis.
At 4 year follow-up, there was a evidence of the necrosis of the femoral head.

claims.text: A 60-year-old woman was in a traffic accident while walking, was in a coma and was taken to a nearby hospital, then shifted to the authors hospital after 2 weeks. On presentation she was conscious, oriented and hemodynamically stable. Radiographs showed ipsilateral left femoral neck (Garden II, nondisplaced) and sub-trochanteric (Seinsheimer IIIB) fractures and a right ulna olecranon fracture, with AIS 14 and ISS 27.
